foundations.title: What is an application?
objectives: Recognize the visible page, the behind-the-scenes logic, and saved data.
Explain why one application can need several programs.

foundations.title: Follow a request
objectives: Follow a request and its response.
Tell an unreachable server from an application error.

foundations.title: Speak HTTP
objectives: Read a simple HTTP request and response status.
Understand what HTTPS protects and what it cannot guarantee.

foundations.title: Find a server by name
objectives: Tell a name from an IP address.
Explain why changing DNS does not start an application.

foundations.title: Choose the right door
objectives: Explain why an address also needs a port.
Distinguish a firewall rule from a listening application.

foundations.title: What runs on a server?
objectives: Distinguish files, processes, CPU, and memory.
Understand the operating system and a safe service account.

foundations.title: Make your first deployment
objectives: Describe deployment as more than uploading files.
Check an app after starting it and restore a working version.

foundations.title: Keep a history with Git
objectives: Explain a repository, commit, branch, and merge.
Distinguish saving locally from publishing or deploying.

foundations.title: Check it before shipping
objectives: Explain what a build produces and what a test checks.
Recognize that passing tests are evidence, not a guarantee.

foundations.title: Build a delivery pipeline
objectives: Read the stages of a CI/CD pipeline.
Distinguish continuous delivery from automatic deployment.

foundations.title: Same app, different settings
objectives: Separate code, configuration, and secrets.
Explain why development, staging, and production need different settings.

foundations.title: Keep the notes when the app stops
objectives: Distinguish temporary memory from persistent storage.
Explain why persistence is not the same as a backup.

foundations.title: Package once, run it again
objectives: Distinguish an image, a container, and a registry.
Understand what still needs to be supplied outside the package.

foundations.title: Share the traffic
objectives: Explain a load balancer and a health check.
Recognize the limits of adding more app copies.

foundations.title: Find clues before changing things
objectives: Distinguish logs from metrics and traces.
Use a symptom, a hypothesis, a small change, and a check.

foundations.title: Why Kubernetes exists
objectives: Connect delivery, runtime, networking, storage, and recovery.
Choose when orchestration helps and when a simpler deployment is enough.

lessons.title: Where does an app live?
objectives: Tell the difference between a browser and a server.
Follow a request from a visitor to an application.

lessons.title: Pack an app into a container
objectives: Distinguish an image from a running container.
Understand what containers package—and what they do not.

lessons.title: Why do we need Kubernetes?
objectives: Explain desired state and reconciliation.
Recognize when Kubernetes adds unnecessary complexity.

lessons.title: Meet the cluster
objectives: Identify nodes and the control plane.
Explain scheduling without assuming every node has room.

lessons.title: Your first Pod
objectives: Understand the relationship between Pods and containers.
Distinguish restarting a container from replacing a Pod.

lessons.title: Keep the app running
objectives: Connect Deployments, replicas, and Pods.
Observe recovery and the gap before a replacement is ready.

lessons.title: Help visitors find the app
objectives: Understand Services and label selectors.
Separate internal service access from public access.

lessons.title: Settings, secrets, and saved notes
objectives: Choose ConfigMaps, Secrets, and persistent storage for different needs.
Avoid confusing encoding with encryption.

lessons.title: Update without the surprise outage
objectives: Explain rolling updates and readiness.
Understand what rollback does and does not restore.

lessons.title: Your first Kubernetes story
objectives: Connect the core concepts without memorizing commands.
Identify a sensible next step toward real Kubernetes practice.

lessons.title: Give everything a clear home
objectives: Use a namespace to narrow your view.
Explain the difference between grouping resources and protecting them.

lessons.title: Leave enough room to run
objectives: Distinguish resource requests from limits.
Tell a placement problem from a memory-limit problem.

lessons.title: Some work should finish
objectives: Choose a Job for work with a completion point.
Understand retries and scheduled work without assuming exactly-once execution.

lessons.title: Read the clues, then make a change
objectives: Use status, events, logs, and a real request together.
Reject a superficial fix that only hides the warning.
